title: Bundesautobahn 2
content: # A 2 (Germany). |  | You can help **expand this article with text translated from the corresponding article "de:A 2 (Germany)") in German**. * You may also add the template `{{Translated|de|A 2 (Germany)}}` to the talk page "Talk:A 2 (Germany)"). `{{Translated|de|A 2 (Germany)}}`. ***Bundesautobahn 2*** (German for 'Federal Motorway 2', short form **Autobahn 2**, abbreviated as **BAB 2** or **A 2**) is an autobahn in Germany that connects the Ruhr area in the west to Berlin in the east. The A 2 was modified in the late 1990s, and completely rebuilt in the former East Germany. In the area of Hanover, it was natural for the motorway to pass shortly to the south of the city. As Hanover was at that time one of the hubs of German air traffic and the airport was in the north of the city, it was decided, however, for a northern bypass of the city.

title: A2 motorway (Switzerland) — Grokipedia
content: The A2 motorway (German: *Autobahn A2*; French: *Autoroute A2*; Italian: *Autostrada A2*), also known as the Gotthard Motorway, is Switzerland's principal north-south highway, spanning approximately 295 kilometers from the German border at Basel in the north to the Italian border at Chiasso in the south.](#ref-1)](#ref-2) It traverses varied terrain, including the Jura Mountains, Swiss Plateau, and Alps, with key engineering feats such as the 16.9-kilometer Gotthard Road Tunnel—the country's longest road tunnel—and the 9.2-kilometer Seelisberg Tunnel, facilitating efficient transalpine passage.](#ref-3) As part of the European route E35, the A2 handles substantial domestic and international transit traffic, underscoring its role as the backbone of Switzerland's road network despite the nation's dense rail infrastructure and ongoing debates over capacity expansions amid persistent congestion, particularly during peak seasons around the Gotthard section.](#ref-4)](#ref-5) The motorway's development, spanning decades with the Gotthard Tunnel opening in 1980, reflects Switzerland's emphasis on reliable overland connectivity for economic freight movement and personal mobility, where empirical traffic data shows roads accommodating over 70% of inland goods transport by volume.](#ref-6).
